questions.question: A fraction bar shows one whole granola bar split into 8 equal parts. 3 of those parts are shaded blue. Which fraction names the shaded amount of the whole granola bar?
questions.explain: The denominator counts all the equal parts in one whole (8) and the numerator counts the shaded parts (3), so the shaded amount is 3/8. A common trap is putting the total on top (8/3) or counting the 5 unshaded parts instead.

questions.question: A fraction bar shows one whole paper strip cut into 4 pieces. Three of the pieces are small and match each other, and the fourth piece is much longer than the other three. One small piece is shaded. Can the shaded piece be named 1/4 of the strip?
options: Yes — the strip has 4 pieces and 1 of them is shaded, so it is 1/4
No — fourths must be 4 equal parts, and these 4 pieces are not the same size
No — a whole has to be cut into at least 5 pieces before you can name a fraction
Yes — it is 1/3, because you count only the 3 small pieces as the whole
questions.explain: A denominator only means something when the whole is cut into equal parts, so 4 unequal pieces are not fourths. The usual trap is just counting pieces and writing 1/4 without checking that the parts match in size.

questions.question: A fraction bar shows one whole loaf of banana bread cut into 6 equal slices. Emma eats 1 slice, so she ate 1/6 of the loaf. What does the denominator 6 tell you?
options: The number of slices Emma ate
The number of pieces of any size the loaf could be broken into, whether or not they match
The number of equal parts the whole loaf is cut into
The number of slices left after Emma eats one
questions.explain: The denominator always tells how many equal parts the whole was split into, and the numerator tells how many of those parts you are talking about. The trap is thinking the bottom number counts pieces of any size, or counts the leftovers.

questions.question: A fraction bar shows one whole ribbon divided into 5 equal parts. 2 of the parts are shaded green and the rest are plain. Which fraction names the part of the ribbon that is NOT shaded?
questions.explain: There are 5 equal parts in the whole, so 5 is the denominator; 5 - 2 = 3 parts are plain, so the unshaded amount is 3/5. The trap is naming the shaded 2/5 instead, or flipping the numbers so the bigger number sits on top.

questions.question: Liam writes 5/12 to show the part of his hockey practice he spent on skating drills. Which sentence tells what the 5 and the 12 mean?
options: The whole practice is split into 12 equal parts and 5 of them are drills
The whole practice is split into 5 equal parts and 12 of them are drills
The whole practice is broken into 12 chunks of any length and 5 of them are drills
5 and 12 are two separate wholes being compared
questions.explain: In 5/12 the bottom number is how many equal parts make one whole and the top number is how many of those parts are counted, so 12 equal parts with 5 of them as drills. The trap is reading the numbers in the wrong order, or forgetting the parts must be equal.

questions.question: Mrs. Poon has one 90 cm ribbon and wants to cut the whole ribbon into thirds so each piece is exactly 1/3. Which cutting really partitions the ribbon into thirds?
options: Three pieces measuring 40 cm, 30 cm and 20 cm
Three pieces measuring 30 cm each
Three pieces of 30 cm cut from the ribbon, with 10 cm left over
Two pieces measuring 45 cm each
questions.explain: Thirds means the whole is used up in 3 equal parts: 90 ÷ 3 = 30 cm each. The trap is counting three pieces of any lengths (40, 30, 20) as thirds, or leaving part of the whole uncut.

questions.question: Noah folds one whole sheet of paper, shades part of it, and writes a fraction with denominator 6 and numerator 1. Which description matches his paper?
options: 6 parts that are not all the same size, with 1 shaded
1 equal part, with 6 parts shaded
6 equal parts, with 1 part shaded
7 equal parts, with 1 shaded
questions.explain: The denominator 6 means the whole sheet is folded into 6 equal parts and the numerator 1 means one of them is shaded. Watch two traps: swapping the two numbers, and accepting 6 parts that are not the same size.

questions.question: A 2 L jug of apple juice is poured out at a school picnic. In which case is each glass exactly 1/8 of the whole jug?
options: The 2 L jug fills 8 glasses, some holding 300 mL and some holding 200 mL
The 2 L jug fills 4 glasses of 500 mL each
Eight glasses of 250 mL are poured from a 3 L jug, with juice left in the jug
The 2 L jug fills 8 glasses of 250 mL each
questions.explain: 2 L = 2000 mL, and 2000 ÷ 8 = 250 mL, so 8 equal glasses of 250 mL each make eighths of the whole jug. The trap is calling any 8 glasses eighths even when they hold different amounts, or when the whole jug is not used up.

questions.question: At a birthday party in Surrey, one whole rectangular cake is cut into 6 pieces: 2 big corner pieces and 4 smaller middle pieces. Priya takes one small middle piece and says, ‘I ate 1/6 of the cake.’ What is the best response?
options: She is wrong — the 6 pieces are not equal, so no single piece is exactly 1/6
She is right — 1/6 just means one piece out of six, no matter the sizes
She is wrong — she ate 1/4, because there are 4 small pieces
She is right — there are 6 pieces and she took 1 of them
questions.explain: A denominator of 6 promises 6 equal parts of the whole cake, and unequal pieces cannot be sixths. The trap is counting pieces instead of checking that every part is the same size.

questions.question: A walking trail at a BC park is 800 m long, and flags split the whole trail into equal sections of 100 m each. Kai walks from the start to the 3rd flag. What fraction of the whole trail has Kai walked?
questions.explain: First find the equal parts: 800 ÷ 100 = 8 sections, so 8 is the denominator; Kai walked 3 of them, giving 3/8. The trap is using 100 (the length of one section) as the denominator, or naming the 5 sections still ahead.

questions.question: Bar A and Bar B are two chocolate bars of exactly the same size. Bar A is broken into 4 equal parts and 1 part is shaded. Bar B is broken into 4 parts where one part is half the whole bar and the other three are small; one small part is shaded. Emma says both shaded parts are 1/4. Which statement is correct?
options: Both show 1/4, because the two bars are the same size to start with
Both show 1/4, because each bar has 4 pieces with 1 piece shaded
Only Bar A shows 1/4, because only Bar A is broken into 4 equal parts
Neither shows 1/4, because the shaded piece has to be the largest piece
questions.explain: A fraction names equal parts of the whole, so only the bar broken into 4 matching parts has pieces worth 1/4. The trap is thinking that any 4 pieces make fourths — on Bar B one small piece is much less than a quarter.

questions.question: For a relay at school, a class of 24 students is split into 6 equal teams. Mia is on one of the teams. Which statement about the fraction of the class that one team makes up is correct?
options: 1/6 — the denominator 6 shows how many students are on each team
1/24 — the denominator 24 shows one team out of 24 students
1/6 names one team even if some teams end up with more students than others
1/6 — the denominator 6 shows the whole class was split into 6 equal teams
questions.explain: The whole class is the whole, split into 6 equal groups, so one team is 1/6 and the denominator counts those equal groups (24 ÷ 6 = 4 students per team, which is not the denominator). Two traps: using the number of students as the denominator, and forgetting the groups must be equal.
